e-4185.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
e-4185.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form $\displaystyle{\sum_{n=1}^N a_1 r^{n-1}},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum $S_N$ of a geometric series:

$$
S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $a_1 = 3,$ $r = 2,$ and $N = 8.$ If we substitute these values into the formula for $S_N,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{8}3(2)^{n-1} & =3\cdot (\frac{1-{2}^{8}}{1-2}) \\  & =3\cdot (\frac{-255}{-1}) \\  & =765\end{aligned}
$$

e-4186.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Simplified Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
e-4186.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form $\displaystyle{\sum_{n=1}^N a r^{n}},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum $S_N$ of a geometric series:

$$
S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r = 4$ and $N = 5.$ We need to figure out the value of $a_1.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
a_n = 3(4)^n,
$$

and therefore we can calculate the first term $a_1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =3(4)^{1} \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute $a_1 = 12,$ $r = 4,$ and $N = 5$ into the formula for $S_N,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{5}3(4)^{n} & =12\cdot \frac{(1-{4}^{5})}{1-4} \\  & =-\frac{12}{3}(-1\,023) \\  & =4\,092\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
content.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=9,$ $r=3$ and $N=6.$ If we substitute these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{6}9(3)^{n-1} & =9\cdot \frac{(1-{3}^{6})}{1-3} \\  & =-\frac{9}{2}(-728) \\  & =3\,276\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=3$ and $N=6.$ We need to figure out the value of ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=5(3)^{n},
$$

and therefore we can calculate the first term ${a}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =5(3)^{1} \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=15,r=3$ and $N=6$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{6}5(3)^{n} & =15\cdot \frac{(1-{3}^{6})}{1-3} \\  & =15\cdot \frac{(1-{3}^{6})}{(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{15}{2}(-728) \\  & =5\,460\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Since the given series is in the form ∑n=1Narn, it is a geometric series.

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum SN of a geometric series. SN=a1(1−rN)1−r

In this case, r=3 and N=6. We need to figure out the value of a1.

The formula for the nth term of the series is

an=5(3)n,

and therefore we can calculate the first term a1 as follows: a1=5(3)1=15

If we substitute a1=15,r=3 and N=6 into the formula for SN, we obtain the following:

∑n=165(3)n=15⋅(1−36)1−3=15⋅(1−36)(−2)=−152(−728)=5460

content.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=3$ and $N=6.$ We need to figure out the value of ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=5(3)^{n},
$$

and therefore we can calculate the first term ${a}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =5(3)^{1} \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=15,r=3$ and $N=6$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{6}5(3)^{n} & =15\cdot \frac{(1-{3}^{6})}{1-3} \\  & =15\cdot \frac{(1-{3}^{6})}{(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{15}{2}(-728) \\  & =5\,460\end{aligned}
$$
